name: Scapular Wall Slides
description: Scapular wall slides are performed with the back flat against a wall, sliding the arms overhead while maintaining contact between the arms and wall throughout. They train thoracic extension, scapular upward rotation, and shoulder flexion in a controlled, low-load manner — making them an essential warm-up, postural correction, and shoulder rehabilitation exercise for overhead athletes.

execution.starting_position: Stand with the back flat against a wall. Feet 10-20 cm away from the wall. Arms bent to 90 degrees at shoulder height, pressed against the wall — forearms and elbows maintaining contact.
execution.setup_instructions: Ensure the entire back — lumbar, thoracic, and head — maintain contact with the wall. This is very challenging for those with thoracic kyphosis.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms at 90-90 position (elbows at shoulder height, bent 90 degrees) against the wall.
Step 2: Slide both arms overhead while maintaining full contact between arms and wall.
Step 3: Try to reach arms overhead to a Y position.
Step 4: Slide back to the 90-90 starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale sliding up. Inhale sliding down.
common_mistakes: Arms losing contact with the wall during the slide — this defeats the purpose
Lumbar hyperextension — back must stay flat throughout
safety_considerations: Appropriate for all fitness levels as a warm-up or mobility tool
Avoid forcing range of motion — work within comfortable limits
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: 90-90 start position to full overhead Y.
coaching_cues: Back flat on the wall at all times
Arms slide — do not lift off
Feel the shoulder blades rotating as the arms go overhead
